title: 15-Minute Chinese Tomato Egg Stir-Fry
hook: The reset dinner after a long holiday weekend: Chinese tomato eggs, one pan, 15 minutes
benefit: High in protein, with vitamin C from the tomatoes and whole grain fiber from the brown rice
ingredients: 4 ripe medium tomatoes (about 1 1/2 lb), cut into 8 wedges each
2 scallions, white and green parts sliced and kept separate
1 tbsp avocado or other neutral oil, divided
2 cups cooked brown rice, warm, for serving
steps: Beat the eggs with the water, 1/4 teaspoon of the salt and the white parts of the scallions until smooth. The splash of water keeps the eggs soft and fluffy.

Heat 2 teaspoons of the oil in a large nonstick skillet or wok over medium-high until it shimmers. Pour in the eggs, let them set for 20 seconds, then push them gently into big soft curds for about 1 minute. Scoop them out while still a little glossy; they finish cooking later.

Add the last teaspoon of oil and the tomato wedges to the same pan. Cook over medium-high, stirring now and then, for 4 to 5 minutes until the tomatoes soften and release their juice. Press a few wedges with the spatula so they break down into a sauce.
Stir in the sugar, soy sauce, the remaining 1/4 teaspoon of salt and the white pepper. Simmer for 1 minute until the sauce is glossy and lightly thickened.

Return the eggs to the pan and fold them gently into the tomatoes for about 1 minute, just until coated and set. Turn off the heat, scatter the scallion greens on top and serve right away over 1 cup of warm brown rice per person.
vo_steps: Beat the eggs with a splash of water, a pinch of salt and the scallion whites.
Soft scramble them in hot oil for about a minute and scoop them out while still glossy.
Cook the tomato wedges four to five minutes until they soften and get saucy.
Stir in the sugar, soy sauce, salt and white pepper and simmer for one minute.
Fold the eggs back in, top with scallion greens and serve over warm brown rice.
